My family has worked this same land for three generations. I know this soil. I know the rains come heavy in July and August but the spring is dry. I know the market buyers come for wheat and corn — always have. At my age, I am not going to try something new and watch it fail. My knees are not good and my second son is in Shijiazhuang now, so I must keep things manageable.

I will plant winter wheat on all 8 mu of my land in October, then after the June harvest, I will plant summer corn on the same plots. This is what everyone in our village does. This is what I have done since I was young. The land here is flat and the water table is still reachable. The grain station buys both crops.

For wheat, I use the improved Jimai 22 variety — our village seed station sells it and my neighbor Mr. Liu has used it for five years with good results. For corn I always use Zhengdan 958, the hybrid seed. You can buy it everywhere and it yields well.

I will apply fertilizer mostly as a base before planting, with one topdressing of urea for the wheat in spring when the soil starts to warm. I irrigate wheat three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. For corn, summer rains usually help so I only irrigate once or twice if it stays dry. I spray herbicide after wheat emerges and again at heading time for aphids and rust. Same for corn — two sprays. I use the rotary tiller my nephew rents out — cheaper than hiring a plough team.

I expect around 450 jin... no, 450 kg per mu for wheat if the weather cooperates, maybe 550 for corn.
